claims.text: Applying a thin, continuous, adherent Al2O3 coating to cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxidation resistance at 1000 °C in air for exposures up to 100 hours.
An Al2O3 coating will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion into HfNbTaTiZr.
Blocking oxygen diffusion will prevent formation of harmful oxides in HfNbTaTiZr.
High-temperature oxidation or oxygen exposure can cause mechanical degradation or embrittlement.
Reducing oxidation-induced degradation with the coating will maintain the mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr.
The coated alloy will retain a yield strength above 163 MPa at 1000 °C.
The coated alloy will retain tensile ductility above 8% at 1000 °C.
The coating will cause only a minimal change in mechanical performance relative to uncoated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The claimed mechanical-performance retention applies at strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1 and temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The coating's effectiveness depends on its thickness, uniformity, and adhesion.
Coating processing and substrate surface preparation can affect coating adhesion and performance.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis promises no compromise or only minimal change in mechanical performance, but the falsification rule permits as much as a 20% decrease relative to the uncoated alloy before declaring failure.

The absolute predictions of yield strength above 163 MPa and ductility above 8% are not incorporated into the falsification rule. The experiment could therefore pass its relative-loss criterion while violating one or both absolute predictions.
